transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Moore (Redwood CSM); Sasha Patel (Tidepool Head of Platform), Jon Reyes (CTO), Priya Singh (Infra), Marco Liu (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick renewal + region activation; pilot in EU; security docs; SOW draft and PO timing.

[00:00:12] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:00:18] Sasha Patel: Yep, loud and clear, Sasha here.
[00:00:20] Jon Reyes: Jon — good to be here.
[00:00:25] Maya Chen: Great. High level agenda: renewal scope, the EU region activation, pilot benchmarks, and security. Diego will walk through the pilot details.
[00:00:34] Diego Alvarez: Thanks Maya. Quick note: Olivia couldn't make it so I took some of the perf numbers. We'll go through expected token throughput, KV cache impact, and burst plan.
[00:00:45] Priya Singh: Quick clar — we did see a couple of intermittent latency spikes last month, so we want to be sure the SLA and fallback routing are nailed down before we commit to extra capacity.
[00:00:56] Lena Moore: Good call. We'll put that in the SOW reliability section.
[00:01:05] Maya Chen: Okay let's start with renewal ask. Sasha, you mentioned earlier you wanted a 12-month extension with a 20% capacity uplift and EU region added — is that still right?
[00:01:16] Sasha Patel: Yeah that's the ask. Our EU customer base has grown and we need lower RTT for the EU app tier, also for data residency. We prefer VPC/private for EU but open to hybrid if the ops tradeoffs are heavy.
[00:01:31] Jon Reyes: Also timeline — we need EU in production by end of Q1. Ideal pilot before holiday push, so mid-November for a verification week.
[00:01:43] Maya Chen: Cool. Diego, can you talk through the options (hosted EU vs VPC private in EU)?
[00:01:50] Diego Alvarez: Sure. Two lanes: 1) Hosted EU: fastest to spin up, Redwood manages infra, regular API keys, standard audit logs. Lower lead time — days to weeks depending on capacity. 2) VPC/private: we deploy a control plane but customer-managed network peering, KMS integration for keys, and audit log shipping to their SIEM. This has more setup (network, peering, KMS, firewall rules) — typically 4–8 weeks. Performance wise both can meet latency targets; VPC adds a bit of network overhead depending on peering. Also we have Dedicated pools if you want reserved capacity to avoid cold routing.
[00:02:34] Priya Singh: Ok, if we do VPC we need KMS integration and HSM compatibility for keys. Is that supported?
[00:02:40] Diego Alvarez: Yes — we support customer KMS (AWS KMS + external HSM patterns). We'll need the key policy and grant flow. We'll include the KMS integration steps in the runbook.
[00:02:49] Marco Liu: From procurement, we need clarity on pricing delta for hosted vs private, and any ongoing infra fees. Also payment terms — PO timing matters.
[00:02:58] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll include a cost sensitivity matrix. Diego: can you highlight where latency vs cost tradeoffs live?
[00:03:05] Diego Alvarez: Sure. The knobs: quantization profile (int8 vs int4), batching window, KV/prefix caching TTLs, and model family choice. Example: switching to int4 reduces cost by ~30% but can add some generation artifacts; larger batching reduces per-token cost but increases p99 latency. We can target 50–100ms p50 with small batches for chat-like flows; if you push for 30–40ms p50 you pay more for reserved Dedicated capacity and smaller latency-optimized kernels.
[00:03:33] Jon Reyes: For us the user-perceived latency is more important on the EU web tier. We can tolerate slightly lower generation quality if the model output is still within acceptance.
[00:03:43] Sasha Patel: We also want to avoid surprises — regression alerts and quality monitors are critical. Can Redwood tie evals to rollouts?
[00:03:50] Diego Alvarez: Yes — Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set evaluations and tie alerts to a deploy. We'll add a canary policy with automatic fallback to previous model if quality drops.
[00:03:58] Priya Singh: On audit/compliance: SOC2 report, encryption in transit+at-rest, and per-token audit logs matter. Do you retain full transcripts by default?
[00:04:08] Lena Moore: We retain call transcripts per account policy; retention is configurable. For enterprise we can set zero retention or customer-only retention. We'll include options in the SOW.
[00:04:16] Marco Liu: Also need a network diagram for VPC peering and an SLA callout for failover.
[00:04:22] Diego Alvarez: We'll include a playbook: primary region EU with auto-fallback to US region, and capacity thresholds for burst. That will be in the runbook.
[00:04:30] Sasha Patel: Sounds good. What's the rough uplift quote ballpark?
[00:04:33] Maya Chen: Preliminary numbers: current commit is 1.2M tokens/mo. A 20% uplift plus dedicated burst buffer and EU region private option would shift the commitment to ~1.5M tokens/mo with a dedicated pool fee. We'll send a detailed SOW with line-item pricing.
[00:04:49] Marco Liu: Need that by early next week ideally to align with our procurement cycle.
[00:04:53] Maya Chen: We'll aim for EOD Nov 5.
[00:04:57] Diego Alvarez: Back to pilot specifics — propose a 1-week pilot where we route a % of EU traffic to the EU region and run end-to-end latency, throughput, and failure-mode tests. We'll also run the eval prompt set to validate quality.
[00:05:12] Jon Reyes: For the pilot we need the exact prompt set and SLOs up front. We'll share the top 50 user flows.
[00:05:18] Diego Alvarez: Great — we'll use that and add synthetic load scripts.
[00:05:23] Sasha Patel: One more question: billing — do you prorate the EU region activation or apply in the next billing period?
[00:05:29] Maya Chen: We can prorate for the first month or include it as a separate line item on the initial invoice. We'll outline options in the SOW.
[00:05:35] Marco Liu: Also need to confirm data residency controls — can we specify that EU user data never leaves EU?
[00:05:41] Diego Alvarez: With VPC/private and region pinning we can keep inference and logs in-region. We’ll need to configure log shipping destination to an EU SIEM. Some metadata (billing metadata) might traverse Redwood control plane in the US unless you elect for private control plane. We'll call that out.
[00:05:58] Priya Singh: Good to call that out.
[00:06:02] Lena Moore: I'll add data residency notes to the SOW.
[00:06:08] Sasha Patel: About SLA — we're looking for p99 latency targets and credits for breaches. What's Redwood's standard?
[00:06:14] Maya Chen: Standard SLA for Dedicated includes 99.9% uptime and latency SLOs per model profile. For enterprise we can negotiate credits and escalation.
[00:06:23] Jon Reyes: Ok, procurement will want the escalation ladder documented.
[00:06:26] Marco Liu: Yup.
[00:06:29] Diego Alvarez: Quick tech note on the perf side — for EU region we recommend enabling KV cache for common prefixes; that can cut token compute by ~18–25% for conversational flows. We'll include recommended TTLs.
[00:06:42] Priya Singh: Do you provide the cache footprint numbers? We need to size memory on our side if we're doing private.
[00:06:48] Diego Alvarez: Yes—I'll include expected KV size per 10k active users and memory consumption estimates for the chosen model family.
[00:06:55] Sasha Patel: On the contractual term, we prefer a 12-month extension with one-time rate hold for the first 6 months. Is that something you can accommodate?
[00:07:02] Maya Chen: We can structure a 12-month contract with a 6-month fixed rate and a review thereafter. I'll draft options.
[00:07:08] Marco Liu: Any discounts for upfront annual payment?
[00:07:11] Maya Chen: Yes — standard is 8–12% for annual up-front, depending on commitment size. We'll model that in the SOW.
[00:07:18] Jon Reyes: For the pilot, what telemetry do you surface? Token breakdown, per-route latency, and error rates?
[00:07:24] Diego Alvarez: All of that plus per-token costing and per-request trace IDs. Redwood Console will show per-model token split and route-level dashboards.
[00:07:33] Priya Singh: Can we get a temporary demo account with EU routing to validate console metrics before pilot?
[00:07:38] Lena Moore: We can provision a short-lived sandbox with EU routing for the SE team to validate. Diego, will you need access?
[00:07:44] Diego Alvarez: Yes — and we'll need sample prompts and a list of user flows.
[00:07:48] Sasha Patel: We'll send that by EOD Nov 3.
[00:07:52] Maya Chen: Great. Anything else on your side?
[00:07:55] Jon Reyes: One small ask — can Redwood include a canary rollback window in the runbook? We want auto-fallback if quality drop > 3% on key prompts.
[00:08:03] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely — will set the canary threshold and automated fallback.
[00:08:07] Maya Chen: Okay let's jump to timeline recap and owners.
[00:08:11] Lena Moore: Recap: SOW by Nov 5, pilot runbook by Nov 10, pilot week Nov 15–22, procurement review and PO sign-off target Nov 12–18.
[00:08:22] Marco Liu: That aligns with our internal timeline.
[00:08:25] Sasha Patel: Quick security item — please attach recent SOC2 Type II cert and any penetration test summary.
[00:08:32] Lena Moore: We'll attach SOC2 and a summary of pen test scope. For deeper infosec review we can set up a security call.
[00:08:40] Priya Singh: If we do private control plane, we'd need a data processing addendum and access controls documented.
[00:08:47] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll include DPA template and RBAC examples.
[00:08:52] Jon Reyes: Curious — are there any capacity constraints in EU due to holiday provisioning?
[00:08:58] Diego Alvarez: We're seeing slight demand from other customers for EU infra in early Dec, but for a 20% uplift we can commit with a short lead time if we get PO in November. If you need higher burst, we might need to provision additional dedicated nodes.
[00:09:12] Sasha Patel: Then we'll aim to get PO in the November window.
[00:09:16] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll close with next steps — Maya will send SOW, Diego to send runbook + benchmark scripts, Priya to send network contacts and prompt flows, Marco to send procurement timing.
[00:09:30] Marco Liu: I'll follow up with PO timeline and any redlines.
[00:09:34] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll target the pilot kickoff planning doc by Nov 10.
[00:09:39] Sasha Patel: Thanks everyone.
[00:09:42] -- end of formal agenda --

[00:28:00] (discussion continues - deep dive details, Diego walks through sample p99 graphs, occasional crosstalk)
[00:35:12] Diego Alvarez: Note on batching — if you set batch window to 10ms you keep p50 low but cost per token goes up. If you move to 50ms, cost drops significantly for high throughput.
[00:42:09] Priya Singh: We want the recommended defaults for our web tier and batch settings.
[00:42:15] Diego Alvarez: I'll include recommended defaults and sensitivity table.
[00:46:30] Maya Chen: Final wrap: action items and owners as discussed. We'll book a security deep-dive next week if needed.
[00:51:45] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors (product names sometimes shortened) and timestamps are approximate.
